image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a grey whale swimming near the surface of green water. The image focuses on the dorsal side of the whale, showing its mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches and callosities. A distinct longitudinal ridge runs along the back. Part of a yellow object (likely a kayak or boat) is visible in the bottom left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head and blowholes are not visible in this cropped dorsal view; only the mid-to-posterior body is shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey coloration with scattered white patches consistent with barnacle/cyamid infestation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no dorsal fin. Instead, a series of low humps (knuckles) is visible trailing down the back, which is a key diagnostic feature of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body appears thick and robust, consistent with the massive scale of a baleen whale relative to the water surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed across the entire visible dorsal surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth and interior of the whale are not visible; baleen plates cannot be seen.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located ventrally/laterally and are submerged or out of frame in this dorsal shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are not visible in this cropped view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Close inspection reveals raised, rough textures (callosities) and irregularities on the skin surface, not just flat color patterns.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The dark line running along the spine appears slightly too uniform and sharp compared to the organic irregularity of natural skin folds, though it could be a shadow. It lacks subtle micro-texture variation.

The yellow object (likely a kayak) has an unnaturally smooth, plastic-like gradient and lacks clear structural definition or interaction with the water (no realistic splash or displacement at the contact point).

To analyze the realism of the skin pores, barnacles, and callosities, checking for AI-smoothing or repetitive texture patterns.
To check for edge bleeding or halo effects where the whale's back meets the water, a common AI artifact in liquid scenes.
